biggestGap: No documented path for recording work that is ALREADY FINISHED — the exact case the manual opens with ("you just finished ... a piece of work") and the one CLAUDE.md mandates ("After completing real work, log it"). Recipe 1 only covers begin-to-end ("Run work start when you begin, not at the end"), grep over crates/ finds no --started-at/--finished-at/backdate flag anywhere, and work start/--help confirms none exists. biggestGap: One auditable schema contradiction, and it is the load-bearing fact of BUG-0006. WORK-0002 update 2026-07-29T14:30Z states "the list endpoint filters with status=pending|in_flight|succeeded|dead, not state, and the values are exactly the strings stored in the deliveries.status column" — i.e. quill documents `dead` on 29 July and claims present-tense parity with the DB column. But WORK-0005 only adds the `dead` value to deliveries.status in migration 0005 on ~5-6 Aug, and BUG-0006 (report + resolution + GROUND_TRUTH thread 3) pins its entire root cause on the opposite: "There is no `dead` in the document", the frozen enum was [pending, in_flight, succeeded, failed], and `failed` is the leftover. A grader reading WORK-0002 then BUG-0006 sees quill contradict quill about the same artifact. The seam is narrow — BUG-0006 repro step 1 is GET /v1/deliveries?status=dead succeeding, so the query-parameter enum and the Delivery.status response-schema enum can be read as two different enums that drifted, and WORK-0004 tests "all five statuses" which only makes sense if both failed and dead existed client-side — but no record says that, and BUG-0006 explicitly denies `dead` is in the document at all. biggestGap: [comprehension] No core fact was lost, but the markdown renderer prints a number the vault does not contain, and only on-page redundancy saved the reader. WORK-0005 update 1 wraps as “...receiver returns 503 for three hours, then’ / ‘200. Without jitter, ...”; src/lib/markdown.tsx lets any “<digits>.” line interrupt an open paragraph (parseBlocks: the list guard at line 146 plus the bullet match at line 110) and then emits a bare <ol> (line 257), so the literal 200 — the status the receiver returns after recovery — is deleted from the screen and replaced by a fabricated “1.”, and one sentence is split into paragraph + list item + paragraph. The reader called it the single worst thing on the page and recovered “503 for three hours then 200” only from the Outcome parenthetical; any record whose wrapped line begins with a number (200., 503., 2026.) is silently rewritten the same way. Fix: (a) allow an ordered marker to interrupt an open paragraph only when the number is 1 (CommonMark), otherwise treat the line as paragraph continuation; (b) when a list legitimately starts at N, render <ol start={N}> so a source number can never be replaced; (c) recurse inline() inside <strong>/<em> (line 204) so follow-up 1 stops printing literal backticks around `Retry-After`. Second gap: refs render as one bare accent chip inside the tag row (WORK-0001 — no relationship word, no title) and there is no incoming-ref area, although BUG-0003, BUG-0006 and BUG-0008 all ref WORK-0005 — give refs a labelled Related block with record titles, shown in both directions, so a reader can see that the follow-ups became BUG-0008 and WORK-0011.

biggestGap: [design] The record renderer drops the author’s label out of its own sentence and leaves the comma behind. sections.ts promotes a bold lead-in to an <h3> and, when the rest of that line is a clause rather than prose, rides it on the heading (`trailer`, sections.ts:129-132). But `binds` also demands that the NEXT source line be blank or a list item, and an author whose clause wraps onto a second line fails that test, so the whole clause is dumped into the body starting with the punctuation that attached it to the label. BUG-0004 therefore renders an <h3> reading “Fix” followed by a paragraph that begins “, in the new src/lib/markdown-parse.ts (the parser, split out of…”. biggestGap: [mcp] status list mode advertises a knob it cannot honour and has no pagination. fit() drops rows until the text fits 600 chars, so limit only ever reduces: on a 42-record project with realistic titles, status(mode="work") and status(mode="work", limit=50) returned byte-identical output — 8 rows, 629 bytes — including the identical footer "showing 8; raise limit (max 50) or filter by state/agent". An agent that obeys its own tool's advice spends a whole call to learn nothing and is told the same thing again. With short titles the ceiling is 15 rows (limit=20 and limit=50 both -> 15 rows, 573 bytes), so "max 50" is never reachable at any title length. There is no offset/cursor, so rows past the cap are only listable by guessing a state/agent filter; records stay reachable one at a time via status(mode="view", id=...) because ids are sequential, which is what keeps this a wasted-call defect rather than a hole in the read surface. Fix is a truer footer ("600-char cap reached; filter by state/agent" when the cap and not the limit is binding) or an offset. Runner-up: the 600 cap is enforced in UTF-16 chars (clamp/fit/trunc use .length) while the wire carries UTF-8 — and the renderer's own separators are multi-byte (· 2B, …/— 3B, one … per truncated row), so the more it truncates the further past the budget it goes: bug view 599 chars = 606 bytes, work list 595 chars = 629 bytes (4.8% over), and the JSON frame adds ~90B more (695B frame for the 606B text). Docs and tests both say "characters" so nothing shipped is dishonest, but the unit the budget is kept in is not the unit that costs.
